gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the only 5 kWh-class kit in the range that ships now, BLUETTI's 5kWh RV Kit, is built around the RV5 Power Hub. That hub is screwed to a wall and wired into an RV's distribution panel (IP20 rating, wood screws, drilling template and distribution-panel wiring pack in the box). Its manual limits solar to 12–50 V, 50 A and 1,800 W max, so the kit's panels can't be strung into a high-voltage string, and the bundle includes only 200–600 W of the 1,800 W the hub can take.
standout_why: I compared five rival pages. StormWatts' '5 kWh-Class Solar Generators Compared on Solar Input' (cited in chat 1, rank 1–2 in both chats) gives full PV voltage windows and series/parallel layouts for the Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus (High-PV 135–450 V; Low-PV 16–60 V, 10.5 A), Anker SOLIX S5000 (11–60 V / 16–165 V), EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 (30–150 V / 11–60 V) and Anker F3800 Plus, but it has no BLUETTI product data and never mentions RV kits. Rivals already cover the Jackery, Anker and EcoFlow mechanism, so I'm not repeating it. EnergySage (cited) gives the Apex 300 a 2,400 W solar maximum with no voltage, says it is AC-only out of the box, and says nothing on wiring. StormWatts' 'Bundle vs Buying Separately' (cited) has no input voltages, no 5 kWh kits and no RV kit. Lights On Labs (cited) would not open (self-signed certificate error), so I couldn't check it. None of the pages I opened says that the 5 kWh BLUETTI kit is a fixed RV install with a 50 V solar ceiling.
decides: This confirms the pick and narrows it. The BLUETTI 5kWh RV Kit + 2/4/6 × 100W (5,120 Wh, 5,000 W, ships now, link price $3,799.05–$4,369.05) is the only one of our kits at about 5 kWh that ships now. It works only for a shopper who will mount and wire the RV5 hub into an RV (or something similar), with panels on the roof wired in parallel at 50 V or less. It is not a portable 'solar generator' you plug appliances into, so it can't be the general pick. For a portable 5 kWh kit, the Jackery Solar Generator 5000 Plus stays the answer. Our portable 5 kWh-class kits (Apex 300 + B300K, Apex 200 + B300K) are pre-orders with dispatch in late January 2027, and the Apex 300 store page says reaching 4,000 W of solar takes the SolarX 4K add-on. List the RV kit as 'best for an RV install, ships now'. The bundled panels are small for 5,120 Wh: at rated output, 5,120 Wh ÷ 600 W = 8.5 h, ÷ 400 W = 12.8 h, ÷ 200 W = 25.6 h of full sun.

findings.label: Solar input (PV1/PV2) voltage range, current and power
findings.value: 12 V to 50 V; 50 A max; 1,800 W max
findings.source_title: Bluetti RV5 User Manual, Specifications (p. 50), ManualsLib
findings.note: This is the 'PV1/PV2 (Solar)' column of BLUETTI's RV5 manual spec table. The ManualsLib copy is the 230 V / 50 Hz edition (p. 49 lists 'AC Output 230V'). The PV rows aren't AC-dependent, but I did not read the US manual. BLUETTI's US RV5 manual PDF (cdn.shopify.com …/RV5_User_Manual_US_EN.pdf, linked from support.bluettipower.com/en-us/products/rv5-b4810) was too large to open. A 50 V ceiling means every panel on the hub has to run in parallel or in short strings. A high-voltage series string is not possible.
